tagline: Through the coast redwoods on ground that will not hold still.
intro: North of Klamath, US 101 runs about twelve miles through Del Norte Coast Redwoods State Park toward Crescent City, among coast redwoods in a park that also holds eight miles of wild Pacific coastline.

Part of the way is Last Chance Grade, first cut as a wagon road in 1894 and laid on its present line in the 1930s. Some of it rests on an earthflow that creeps about two inches a year, and the road has since shifted some 40 feet sideways and 30 feet vertically. It is the only road between Crescent City and Humboldt County, and the way around is 449 miles longer.

moments.title: Del Norte Coast Redwoods State Park
moments.text: Set aside in 1925 and about half old-growth coast redwood, the park takes in the highway's whole scenic stretch.

moments.title: Last Chance Grade
moments.text: Three miles lined with redwoods and open to the ocean, propped by more than two dozen retaining walls, where Caltrans has proposed a 6,000-foot tunnel to go underneath.

practical: Last Chance Grade is prone to landslides and slipouts and has been closed at times.
